key_insight: A graph-based spatio-temporal model of breast MRI trajectories can better predict treatment response by learning how imaging changes across multiple timepoints.
clinical_relevance: More accurate prediction of pathological complete response after neoadjuvant chemotherapy could help support more individualized treatment planning in breast cancer.
method: Uses a graph neural network to model relationships across longitudinal DCE-MRI scans
Adds three self-supervised objectives to learn treatment trajectory representations
Tests the effect of number of timepoints and inter-scan time differences
evidence_signal: Evaluated on 585 ISPY-2 patients, the method outperformed vision and self-supervised baselines across several classification metrics.
watch_item: Performance depends on multi-timepoint longitudinal imaging data, so real-world deployment may be limited where scans are sparse or acquisition timing is inconsistent.
paper_title: Graph Representation Learning of Longitudinal Medical Imaging Trajectories for Treatment Response Prediction
